stage: what the runtime hash costs, and why the precise scope needs a new contract

result.the_cost: RuntimeSourceHash takes 0.7 ms per call over the real tree (twenty-one authored files), measured over five passes, so comparing it before and after a compile is essentially free
result.the_decisive_evidence: I looked for a precise mapping from a selection to its runtime FILES inside the compiled pack itself, because that would settle the scope question. THE PACK DOES NOT CARRY ONE: its dependencyGraph is MODULE level (nodes are module ids, edges are module dependencies), and both moduleFingerprints and campaignFingerprint are values the COMPILE DERIVES - so hashing any of them would change on a legitimate compile, which is exactly what Codex ruled out
result.so_the_options_are: (a) the scope implemented today: every authored runtime file, correct but with a false-stale when another campaign changes, and it costs 0.7 ms; (b) a precise scope, which needs a NEW contract that maps a campaign or world selection to its runtime files - the manifest names scene IDS and the pack names MODULE IDS, so neither answers it today
result.the_recommendation: keep (a) for now: it closes the real gap (a world plot edited during a compile no longer slips past), it is cheap, and the false-stale cost is a wasted compile rather than a wrong scene. Switch to (b) when the mapping exists
